A1.justification: Both 29-page PDFs describe the same ProLong study. Their main text, figures, tables, mathematical content, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original ProLong training experiments, benchmark results, and ablations, including Table 10 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experimental results, including HELMET and NoCha evaluations, training ablations, and long-document QA examples.

M1.justification: ProLong’s continued-training procedure, data mixing, RoPE settings, document masking, and UltraChat SFT are unchanged (Section 6, Table 9, Appendix A).

E1.justification: Training data sources and evaluated tasks remain identical, including HELMET, NoCha, RULER, ∞Bench, short-context benchmarks, and the Appendix D examples.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding comparison, including the frontier models in Tables 10 and 12 and the Fu et al. (2024) comparison in Table 24.

E3.justification: Training budgets, context lengths, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are identical, including the settings documented in Table 9 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: The data-mixture, training-length, RoPE, document-mask, initialization, and SFT ablations are unchanged. The supplementary analyses and Appendix D case studies are also retained without revision.

E5.justification: Figure 2 reports means and standard deviations over two training runs in both versions. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples match across the main text and appendices. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The dependency-count argument in Section 4 and RoPE scaling expression in Appendix B.1 are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, takeaway box, and conclusion retain the same claims about the training recipe, SFT on short instructions, 128K performance, and 512K context support.

C2.justification: Interpretations of data-mixture effects, longer-context training, and synthetic SFT are identical. Limitations concerning resources, model scale, generalizability, and benchmark overfitting are unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and training-time information, synthetic-data prompts, and code/data/model access information are unchanged. The added funding acknowledgment supplies no new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Related work, cited research, bibliography entries, and contribution positioning are identical.

P1.justification: v4 adds 'Cisco Research' to the funding acknowledgments on page 12 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All other prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–4, Tables 1–27, captions, placement, and page structure are unchanged. The acknowledgment edit only reflows text within the existing paragraph.

improvement.justification: Adding Cisco Research to the acknowledgments makes funding attribution more complete, but the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged. This administrative update does not produce a meaningful overall quality difference.
